newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, Japanese in talks over parts - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, Japanese in talks over parts - WSJ.

text.p: Boeing Co is negotiating agreements with Japanese manufacturers to produce wing parts for its new 747-X superjumbo jets, The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.

Boeing executives attending Britain's Farnborough International Air Show told the newspaper the talks were with Japan's Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd, Fuji Heavy Industries Ltd and Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd.
The talks would not assure Boeing of any orders for the two planned larger and longer-range 747s that the jet maker hopes to launch formally this year.

However, Boeing's close relationship with those manufacturers in the past is believed to have helped the plane maker win orders from carriers such as Japan Airlines Co Ltd and All Nippon Airways Co Ltd.

Boeing officials are discussing agreements with the Japanese companies that would call for them to build flight-control surfaces, such as flaps and slats, as well as landing-gear doors and the fairing that surrounds the point where the wing and body are joined.
The agreements could be complete in one to two months.
